rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Big Idea match (judge-owned criterion, not a numbered compendium rule — file has no ## Big Idea of its own; checked against the module file that owns this material's Big Idea, earn-the-trust.md)
rules_evaluated.evidence: File is a supplementary reference page — no `## Big Idea` of its own (correctly: Big Idea is a module-file convention, owned here by `earn-the-trust.md`). Checked against that module's Big Idea ("earn your staff engineer's and CISO's trust on a small piece you're shipping this week... Two curated skills from the frontier do the security work") and the strategy doc's M3-detail framing ("Discipline installed before M5's long-running send-off, so you never feel exposed"; "What M3 refuses: frame Q+S as compliance"). The trifecta file's own closer — "Cutting a leg is ordinary engineering" / "Three legs. Cut one." — reinforces the same not-compliance, ordinary-engineering framing rather than contradicting or restating M3's Big Idea. No drift.

File is wired twice into the mood arc (per its own maintainer block: `earn-the-trust.md ## Next` at M3's close — mood 'earned trust' — and `run-the-first-experiment.md ## Send the task off` at M4's send-off gate — mood 'curious readiness'). Both firings reuse near-identical three-question-check language already established in the module files ("Does the agent hold private data?... Does untrusted content reach its context window?... Is there a channel out?"), so the second firing reads as reinforcement of known material rather than new-content teaching load right before the M4 send-off — consistent with §1's teaching-vs-setup distinction. The file's own register ("the check takes a minute," "cutting a leg is ordinary engineering") matches the strategy doc's explicit M3 refusal of compliance-dread framing and the 'you never feel exposed' promise, rather than flattening earned-trust into anxiety.

Framing throughout is structural/diagnostic, not blame-laden: "Audit any agent deployment for the three legs... The check takes a minute"; "Most agent setups assemble all three without anyone deciding to" (describes a pattern to notice, not a mistake the reader is presumed to have already made). No "you did this wrong" phrasing anywhere; the unease on offer is "do I currently have this?" (not-knowing), matching §2's not-knowing/not-having-done-wrong split.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Lead with discipline, not failure mode
rules_evaluated.evidence: No `## Big Idea` / `## Key Concepts` / `## What You'll Learn` heading on this file, so assessed against general body framing. Section leads and the closing kicker lead with the fix, not the failure: "Removing any one leg breaks the trifecta" (heading 4), "Cutting a leg is ordinary engineering" (body lead), "Three legs. Cut one." (closer). Failure vocabulary ("leak," "attacker," "exploit") appears only as structural description of the mechanism being defended against, never as a title or as the training's own coined Big-Idea framing. Title "The lethal trifecta" is Willison's attributed field term ("Simon Willison's frame," line 5), cited verbatim as established vocabulary rather than authored by the training — same curated-vocabulary carve-out class as STRIDE's name.

Sequencing and phrasing match the strategy doc and the wiring module files closely. "The two audits compose. The access-surface map and the STRIDE pass you ran on the feature still hold" correctly presumes M3 Ex1/Ex2 already complete (this page's first firing sits at M3's close, after both exercises) — matches the strategy doc's S-first-then-Q M3 shape and `earn-the-trust.md`'s own Ex1/Ex2 naming verbatim ("Map the access surface," "Threat-model with STRIDE"). The three-question check and "cut one leg" language are near-verbatim identical across all three artifacts (this file, `earn-the-trust.md ## Next`, `run-the-first-experiment.md ## Send the task off`) — no drift, no front-run of M4/M5/M6 content (no mention of gap analysis, plan.md, verifiers, or packaging — all M4–M6 teaching moments owned elsewhere). The maintainer note correctly scopes composition with 'blast-radius' (banked elsewhere, in `how-the-best-do-ci-cd.md`) as an accident-model contrast without importing or redefining that term into this file's body.
